source: Jensen, Hennequin, Mattar (2024) A recurrent network model of planning explains hippocampal replay and human behavior
finding: A meta-RL recurrent agent plans by sampling imagined action sequences (rollouts) from its own policy. These rollouts look like rodent replay.
numbers: 100 GRUs; up to 8 imagined actions per rollout; 120 ms per rollout vs 400 ms per physical action; 8x10^6 training episodes; 5 agents; 94 human participants (Prolific), 4x4 periodic maze
quote: the ability to plan by sampling imagined action sequences from its own policy
limits: Task is a small maze. Policy cannot change at test time without network updates. Local replays only.
agent_relevance: Closest formal bridge: replay as policy-sampled imagined rollouts, which is what an LLM agent does when it simulates steps before acting.

source: Jensen et al. (2024) rodent reanalysis of Widloski and Foster data
finding: Model signatures were found in rat replay: replays avoid walls and over-represent the goal.
numbers: 37 sessions from 3 rats (17, 12, 8), 187-333 neurons per session; both effects P<0.001; home-trial success prob 0.622 for true goal vs 0.403 disjoint control and 0.433 full control; goal over-representation grows over consecutive replays (2nd/3rd vs 1st: P=0.068, P=0.009)
limits: Replay defined as at least 3 adjacent decoded locations in 75 ms windows. Away-trial effect absent (P=0.129).
agent_relevance: Rollouts that are goal-biased and constraint-aware are the useful kind; unbiased random rollouts are not.

source: Jensen et al. (2024) human thinking time vs agent rollouts
finding: More agent rollouts reduce steps to goal. Agent rollout probability tracks human thinking time, weakly.
numbers: r=0.186+-0.007 (chance 0+-0.004); r=0.070+-0.006 after controlling distance to goal; agent thinking about 50 ms shorter; steps to goal fell monotonically up to at least 15 forced rollouts; human RT fell 6.8% and reward rose 7.6% from first to last five episodes
limits: Correlation is small. Thinking time is an estimate; 0.6% of decisions set to 0.
agent_relevance: Supports a budgeted think-before-act operator: more simulation helps, and the amount of thinking should scale with difficulty.

source: Jensen et al. (2024) successful vs unsuccessful rollouts
finding: A successful imagined rollout raises the chance the agent takes its first simulated action. An unsuccessful one lowers it. Same pattern found in rat home trials.
numbers: home trials P<0.001 for first replayed action matching next physical action, successful vs unsuccessful
limits: Effect absent on away trials. Rat task was not a reaction-time task.
agent_relevance: Rollout outcome should gate the commit decision: accept the plan if simulation succeeded, reject otherwise (verify-then-commit).

source: Brain-Like Replay Naturally Emerges in Reinforcement Learning Agents (2024)
finding: A modular agent (CNN encoder, GRU world model HF, RNN policy PFC) develops replay-like multi-step message passing from HF to PFC after reward, without being told to replay.
numbers: 5x5 arena; reward 0.5 checkpoint then 1.0 goal; reward memory k=10; replay with 2 and 6 steps tested; PFC replay lives in about 2-D subspace (70% variance threshold), 3-D at context switch
limits: No numeric gains reported, only figure trends. Single task. HF and PFC fully separated during movement (biologically implausible). Did not analyze reverse replay. Replay metric is author-defined.
agent_relevance: Shows a world-model-to-policy channel that opens only at pauses; fits a scaffold where simulation runs between acts, not during.

source: Brain-Like Replay Naturally Emerges (2024) ablations
finding: Blocking HF-to-PFC flow hurts reward. Reverse direction does not. Masking more replay steps hurts. Shuffling message order barely matters. Multi-step replay beats one-step emission.
numbers: no numbers given in text; trends in Fig 3 and Fig 8; seeds 1-4
limits: Qualitative only. Authors cite Kaefer et al 2020 PFC replay independent of hippocampus, which conflicts with model premise.
agent_relevance: Order of simulated steps may matter less than their content and count: a cheap test for any LLM replay loop.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
finding: Letting an LLM reason offline about a context before any query arrives (a preplay/replay analogue) cuts test-time compute and can raise accuracy.
numbers: about 5x less test-time compute for same accuracy on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME; up to +13% (GSM-Symbolic) and +18% (AIME) with more sleep-time compute; 2.5x lower cost per query on Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic
limits: Abstract-only read. Benefit correlates with how predictable the query is. SWE agent part is only a case study.
agent_relevance: Strongest direct LLM analogue to offline replay and preplay: precompute likely sub-questions while idle. Fits an anticipation state before the task arrives.

source: Momennejad et al. (2023) CogEval: evaluating cognitive maps and planning in LLMs
finding: Eight LLMs tested on cognitive-map and planning tasks taken from human experiments. They look competent on simple structures but fail on harder ones, hallucinating invalid paths and looping.
numbers: 8 models: GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo, davinci-003, Bard, Cohere-xlarge, Claude-1, LLaMA-13B, Alpaca-7B; per-model scores not on the page
quote: do not support the idea of emergent out-of-the-box planning ability in LLMs
limits: Abstract-only read. 2023 models; no numbers captured.
agent_relevance: Same task family as hippocampal planning studies. The scaffold must supply a map and verify paths, because models do not simulate routes reliably alone.

source: Whittington, Warren, Behrens (2021) Relating transformers to models and neural representations of the hippocampal formation
finding: Transformers with recurrent position encodings develop place-cell and grid-cell-like tuning, and are linked to the Tolman-Eichenbaum machine.
numbers: no numbers on abstract page; v1 Dec 2021, v2 Mar 2022
limits: Abstract-only read. Replay is not mentioned on the page.
agent_relevance: Argues LLM architecture and hippocampal models are cousins, so replay-like phenomena may be testable inside transformers.

source: Andrychowicz et al. (2017) Hindsight Experience Replay
finding: Relabel failed trajectories with the goal actually reached, so sparse binary rewards still teach. Works with any off-policy RL.
numbers: robot arm push, slide, pick-and-place; sim-to-real transfer reported; no success rates on abstract page
limits: Abstract-only read. Needs a goal-conditioned setup.
agent_relevance: Machine analogue of replay that learns from failed runs; an LLM agent can restate a failed attempt as a solution to a different goal.

source: Yu et al. (2025) Dyna-Think: Synergizing Reasoning, Acting, and World Model Simulation in AI Agents
finding: Dyna-style agent that simulates the world around planned actions inside its reasoning. Matches R1 best-of-n with far fewer tokens; better world modeling correlates with better agent performance.
numbers: 2x fewer tokens on average than R1; benchmarks OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena; no success rates on page
limits: Abstract-only read. Needs training (imitation and Dyna training), not scaffold-only.
agent_relevance: Evidence that simulating consequences before acting is a usable and cheaper form of thinking.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Agent induces reusable workflows from past episodes (consolidation of experience) and reuses them, offline or online.
numbers: Mind2Web +24.6% relative success; WebArena +51.1% relative; online gain over baselines grows from 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as train-test gap widens; 1000+ tasks, 200+ domains
limits: Abstract-only read. Per-setting tables not read.
agent_relevance: Replay as consolidation into schemas; its gain growing under distribution shift supports abstracting replays rather than storing raw ones.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: Agent gathers experiences on training tasks, extracts natural-language insights, and recalls both at inference without weight updates. Performance improves as experience accumulates.
numbers: no numbers on abstract page; AAAI-24
limits: Abstract-only read.
agent_relevance: Training-free replay loop: store past trajectories, distil rules, recall at decision time.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: Agent verbally reflects on failed attempts and keeps the text in an episodic buffer for the next try. This is a reverse-replay-like credit step done in words.
numbers: 91% pass@1 on HumanEval vs 80% for GPT-4 baseline
limits: Abstract-only read. ALFWorld figure not confirmed on page. Needs a reliable feedback signal.
agent_relevance: Closest existing LLM version of post-outcome replay with credit assignment; already in many agent loops.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager
finding: Minecraft agent keeps a growing library of executable skills learned from experience and reuses them, with no fine-tuning.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior best
limits: Abstract-only read. One game, GPT-4 black box.
agent_relevance: Stores successful traces as reusable sequences, like consolidated replay of rewarded paths.

source: Ma et al. (2026) BrainMem: Brain-Inspired Evolving Memory for Embodied Agent Task Planning
finding: Training-free working, episodic and semantic memory, with post-episode LLM summarization into guidelines. Raises success across planners and four embodied benchmarks.
numbers: EB-ALFRED GPT-4o 56.3 to 75.0; Claude-3.5-Sonnet 64.0 to 74.7; Gemini-1.5-Pro 62.3 to 75.3; EB-Navigation Gemini 24.3 to 61.0 (+36.7); EB-Manipulation about +17-18 points; tokens about 1.4x
limits: No separate replay step and no isolated replay result. Read first 100k of 109k characters.
agent_relevance: Shows consolidation-style memory gives large gains and costs only about 1.4x tokens.

source: Ma et al. (2026) BrainMem ablations
finding: Each memory layer adds accuracy; failure-derived and insight content matter most.
numbers: EB-ALFRED Base, GPT-4o: none 64.0, +working 68.0, +episodic 70.0, +semantic 76.0, +feedback 82.0; without failure reasons 74.0; without learning insights 72.0; working window 1 gives 72.0, 3 gives 82.0, 8 gives 76.0; top-k 1 gives 74.0, k>=2 gives 82.0
limits: One subset; 2-point steps suggest about 50 tasks, so noise is large.
agent_relevance: Replaying failures with reasons is worth more than replaying successes; too long a window hurts.

source: Kim (2025) Teaching AI to Remember: Brain-Inspired Replay in Continual Learning
finding: Internal replay lowers forgetting on CIFAR-100 class-incremental, especially with Synaptic Intelligence, but lowers initial task accuracy and increases overlap between task representations.
numbers: no metrics on abstract page
limits: Not an LLM. Abstract-only read.
agent_relevance: Warns of a replay trade-off: stability gained at the cost of task-specific differentiation.

source: Gu et al. (2026) FSFM: Selective Forgetting of Agent Memory
finding: Biologically inspired forgetting policy for agent memory. Cites hippocampal consolidation only as inspiration; no replay mechanism.
numbers: +8.49% access efficiency; +29.2% signal-to-noise; 100% security risk removal (abstract, controlled experiments)
limits: No benchmark named on page; self-reported.
agent_relevance: Replay needs a forgetting partner; pruning stale entries is part of consolidation.

source: Bhardwaj (2026) SuperLocalMemory V3.3
finding: Local agent memory with forgetting curve, seven retrieval channels including a consolidation channel and Hopfield associative retrieval.
numbers: LoCoMo zero-LLM mode 70.4% (V3.3) vs 74.8% (V3.2); +23.8 multi-hop and +12.7 adversarial points vs V3.2; forgetting curve 6.7x discriminative power
limits: Single author, abstract-only read, consolidation mechanism not explained.
agent_relevance: Brain labelling at marketing level; weak evidence that neuro-inspired memory channels help.

source: Mattar and Daw (2018) Prioritized memory access explains planning and hippocampal replay
finding: Replay order is chosen by gain times need (how much a backup improves policy, times how often the state will be visited). Explains forward and reverse replay. PDF could not be parsed this session, so details are from recall.
numbers: not verified this session
limits: Fetch returned compressed PDF only. Theory uses Dyna-like tabular agents.
agent_relevance: Gives a priority rule for which simulations an agent should run first: high gain, high need.

source: Sagiv, Akam, Witten, Daw (2025) Prioritizing replay when future goals are unknown
finding: Search snippet only: replay targets goals or other states depending on how likely those states are to matter later.
numbers: none seen
limits: Snippet from search result, page not opened.
agent_relevance: Suggests splitting idle compute between current goal and likely future goals, as sleep-time compute does.

source: Bakermans et al. (2025) Constructing future behavior in the hippocampal formation through composition and replay
finding: Search snippet only: simulations plus recordings show that composition and replay build future behavior.
numbers: none seen
limits: Snippet only, page not opened.
agent_relevance: Composition of known sub-sequences is the part an LLM scaffold can copy via skill libraries.

source: Search check: LLM studies directly testing preplay or replay recording paradigms
finding: No paper found that runs an LLM on a Foster-Wilson or Pfeiffer-Foster style paradigm. Web search budget ran out and the arXiv API returned 429, so absence is not proven.
numbers: about 6 targeted searches or fetches, 0 direct hits
limits: Search was thin.
agent_relevance: Our agent claim rests on analogy (sleep-time compute, reflection, skill libraries), not direct tests.

source: Semantic Scholar query: brain-inspired replay consolidation LLM agent memory
finding: Results were dominated by 2025-2026 agent-memory papers with biological labels (SuperLocalMemory, BrainMem, FSFM, brain-inspired replay in continual learning, Hebbian agent memory), mostly self-reported and low-cited.
numbers: 8 results, citation counts 0-4
limits: Citation counts are from one API call.
agent_relevance: A crowded but unvalidated area; prefer methods with ablations such as BrainMem and Sleep-time compute.

source: Jensen et al. (2024) boundary conditions of the rollout model
finding: Authors flag that disengaged nonlocal replays (Olafsdottir et al.) are filtered out and that replay count is less causal in a non-reaction-time rat task.
numbers: time differences capped at 15 s; 10,000 permutations (50,000 for some RL tests); 50,000 episodes for performance comparisons
limits: Network-size lists differ between Methods (60, 80, 100) and Extended Data Fig 4 (60, 100, 140).
agent_relevance: Not every replay is planning. Only goal-relevant, local rollouts should count as thinking steps.
